nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Drives growth in the forest canopy and the grassy clearings and scrub left by past disturbance.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Annual rainfall is about 1,400 to 1,800 mm, falling mostly from May to October. The area also feeds many rivers, including Mekong tributaries.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Holds the nutrients that the evergreen and semi-evergreen forest draws on, and is refilled by decomposers.

nodes.name: Mineral salt lick
nodes.desc: The Poung Nyied salt lick draws sambar and other animals from a wide area, giving them minerals.

nodes.name: Bamboo & forest grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses and bamboo grow in clearings, gaps and secondary growth. Grass is a regular food of large deer such as sambar.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Forest figs bear fruit that many monkeys, apes and birds feed on.

nodes.name: Chestnut-oaks
nodes.desc: Evergreen nut-bearing trees of Southeast Asian hill forest. Their nuts are a mast food for bears and other animals.

nodes.name: Sambar
nodes.desc: A big deer that eats grasses, foliage, fruit and shrubs. It gathers at the Poung Nyied salt lick and is the main named prey of the reserve.

nodes.name: Indian muntjac
nodes.desc: A small forest deer, also called barking deer, that eats leaves, fruit and shoots.

nodes.name: Northern white-cheeked gibbon
nodes.desc: A tree-dwelling ape that eats mainly fruit with some leaves and buds. About 57 groups were estimated in this reserve in 2019.

nodes.name: Stump-tailed macaque
nodes.desc: A forest monkey recorded in the reserve that eats fruit, seeds and leaves.

nodes.name: Asian black bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats fruit, nuts and acorns, insects and larvae, and carrion.

nodes.name: Greater hog badger
nodes.desc: A rooting forest omnivore that feeds on invertebrates and plant matter in leaf litter.

nodes.name: Red-whiskered bulbul
nodes.desc: The best-recorded bird in the surrounding area. It eats fruit and insects, and spreads seeds.

nodes.name: Longhorn beetles
nodes.desc: Wood-boring beetle larvae chew into trunks and stems, and adults feed on nectar and fruit. Several species are recorded nearby.

nodes.name: Leopard cat
nodes.desc: A small forest cat that eats small mammals and birds. Recorded in camera traps in the area.

nodes.name: Asian golden cat
nodes.desc: A medium forest cat listed among the reserve's wildlife. It takes birds and small mammals.

nodes.name: Pearson's horseshoe bat
nodes.desc: One of many insect-eating bats recorded in the forest. It hunts flying insects at night.

nodes.name: Asian water monitor
nodes.desc: A large lizard that hunts a wide range of prey and often eats carrion, helping clean up dead animals.

nodes.name: Tiger
nodes.desc: Once the top predator here, with sambar as a main prey. There have been no park records since 2013, so it is now considered lost from Laos.

nodes.name: Clouded leopard
nodes.desc: A tree-climbing cat of dense forest, recorded in the reserve's evergreen forest. It hunts deer and other mammals.

nodes.name: Dhole
nodes.desc: A pack-hunting wild dog that mainly takes medium and large deer and boar. It has been studied in this reserve and is hit hard by snaring.

nodes.name: Fungi, termites & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and dead animals and return nutrients to the soil.
